C: Celsius. The metric temperature scale used in aviation worldwide for reporting temperature, dew point, and atmospheric conditions; water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard pressure.
CALM: Calm. A wind condition reported in METAR and aviation weather observations when wind speed is less than 1 knot; indicates no significant wind is present at the surface.
CAP: Capacity. The maximum amount of payload, fuel, or passengers an aircraft can carry; also refers to the maximum throughput of an airport, runway, or airspace sector.
CAR: Cargo. Freight, goods, or merchandise transported by aircraft, as distinct from passengers and baggage; may include specialized cargo such as hazardous materials, perishables, or oversized items.
CB: Cumulonimbus. A dense, towering vertical cloud type (ICAO classification) associated with thunderstorms, heavy precipitation, hail, lightning, and severe turbulence; a critical aviation weather hazard requiring avoidance.
CBR: Cumulonimbus with radar. A term used in aviation weather reports indicating that cumulonimbus clouds have been detected or observed using weather radar systems, confirming the presence of convective activity.
CCTV: Closed circuit television. A video surveillance system used at airports and aviation facilities for security monitoring of airside areas, terminals, perimeters, and restricted zones.
CEL: Ceiling. The height above ground level of the lowest cloud layer that is reported as broken or overcast; a critical parameter for instrument approach minima and VFR flight operations.
CEN: Centre. A central facility or location, such as an area control centre, operations centre, or the geographic midpoint of a defined area in aviation operations.
CH: Channel. A specific frequency band or communication path used for voice or data link communications between air traffic control and aircraft, or between aviation facilities.
CHG: Change. A modification or alteration to a flight plan, clearance, weather condition, or operational status; used in NOTAM text and ATC communications to indicate updated information.
CIA: Chemical impact area. A designated area where chemical contamination or hazardous material may be present, requiring special procedures for aircraft operations and personnel safety.
CIG: Ceiling. The height above ground level of the lowest cloud layer reported as broken or overcast; an essential weather parameter for determining instrument flight conditions and approach minima.
CISS: Computerized IFR en-route system. An automated system that processes and manages IFR flight plan data along en-route segments, providing controllers with flight progress information and conflict detection.
CL: Centerline. The imaginary longitudinal line that runs exactly along the midpoint of a runway, taxiway, or airway; marked by painted lines on runways and taxiways for visual guidance.
CLAM: Clearance and delivery. The ATC position or frequency responsible for issuing IFR clearances to departing aircraft and relaying departure instructions prior to pushback and taxi.
CLCT: Collect. A term used in aviation communications and documentation to indicate the gathering or accumulation of data, fees, payments, or information.
CLD: Cooled. A status indicator for equipment or materials that have been reduced in temperature; used in NOTAM text and maintenance documentation to describe the condition of aircraft systems or components.
CLR: Clear(s) or cleared or clearance. An ATC authorization for an aircraft to proceed under specified conditions, or the absence of cloud cover in weather reporting; also used to indicate clearance from obstacles or other traffic.
CLSN: Collision. An event in which two aircraft, or an aircraft and an obstacle or terrain, come into contact; collision avoidance is a primary function of TCAS, ATC separation services, and see-and-avoid procedures.
CMA: Control area. A defined volume of controlled airspace extending upward from a specified altitude above the ground, established to provide air traffic control services to IFR flights within its boundaries.
CMN: Common. A shared frequency, resource, or point used by multiple aircraft or facilities; common frequencies are used for airport advisory, UNICOM, and air-to-air communications.
CMP: Cumulative. The total or accumulated value of a parameter over time, such as cumulative flight time, cumulative fuel consumption, or cumulative exposure to operational factors.
CMS: Climb missile sector. A designated airspace sector or area where missile launch and climb operations are conducted, typically restricted during launch windows to ensure safety of air traffic.
CN: Commission. The act of placing an aviation facility, navigation aid, or system into official operational service after testing and certification.
CNL: Cancel or cancellation. An instruction or notification to terminate a flight plan, clearance, NOTAM, or other aviation action; pilots must explicitly cancel IFR flight plans upon landing VFR.
CNS: Communications, navigation and surveillance. The three core functional areas of air traffic management infrastructure; communications enable voice/data exchange, navigation provides position guidance, and surveillance tracks aircraft positions.
CNTR: Centre. A central ATC facility or location such as an area control centre (ACC) responsible for managing air traffic within a specified flight information region or airspace sector.
CNTRLN: Centerline. The marked longitudinal axis of a runway or taxiway, indicated by painted stripes, that provides directional guidance to pilots during takeoff, landing, and ground movement.
COL: Column. A vertical arrangement of data, values, or aircraft in formation; also refers to a control column in the cockpit used for pitch and roll inputs.
COMM: Communication. The exchange of information between pilots and air traffic control, or between aviation facilities, via voice radio or data link for the safe and efficient conduct of flight.
COMP: Compass. An aircraft instrument that indicates direction relative to magnetic north; a fundamental navigation instrument that provides heading reference for flight operations.
CON: Concerning. A term used in aviation communications and documentation to indicate the subject or topic of a message, instruction, or report.
CONF: Conference. A multi-party communication session involving multiple ATC facilities, aircraft, or aviation stakeholders for coordinated decision-making and information sharing.
CONV: Converge or convergence. The meeting or merging of aircraft, air routes, or air traffic flows at a common point or within a defined airspace area, requiring careful separation management.
COOR: Coordination. The exchange of information and agreement between air traffic control facilities, or between ATC and other aviation entities, to ensure safe and efficient aircraft separation and handoffs.
COP: Change-over point. A defined point along an airway or route at which an aircraft navigating by reference to ground-based NAVAIDs is expected to transfer its primary navigation reference from the facility behind to the facility ahead.
COR: Correct or correction. An amendment to a previous communication, clearance, or data entry; used in ATC phraseology to retract and replace an earlier instruction or information.
CORR: Corridor. A defined airspace channel or route, often with specific lateral and vertical dimensions, designated for a particular type of operation such as military training, special use, or border crossing.
COT: Cargo on tail. A configuration in which cargo is loaded into the tail section of an aircraft, affecting the aircraft's center of gravity and requiring specific weight and balance calculations.
CP: Cap. An altitude or flight level that serves as the upper limit of an airspace sector, control area, or altitude reservation; also refers to the ceiling of a cloud layer or instrument procedure.
CPDLC: Controller-pilot data link communications. A digital text-based communication system that enables controllers and pilots to exchange clearances, instructions, and information via data link, reducing voice channel congestion and improving message accuracy.
CPN: Corporation. A legal business entity involved in aviation operations, such as an airline corporation, airport authority, or aviation service provider.
CRA: Civil reserved airspace. A volume of airspace reserved for specific civil aviation activities, such as flight testing, special operations, or training, where access may be restricted to non-participating traffic.
CRCO: Central route charges office. The ICAO-affiliated body (based in Brussels) responsible for calculating and collecting en-route air navigation service charges for aircraft operating over member states.
CRS: Course. The intended direction of flight measured in degrees relative to a reference (true north or magnetic north); used in navigation to define the desired track between waypoints or along an airway.
CRSA: Course sector antenna. A directional antenna component of a navigation aid system that transmits signals defining a specific course or radial, used in instrument approach and en-route navigation systems.
CRST: Crest. The highest point of a ridge, hill, or mountain; used as a visual reference in VFR navigation and as an obstacle clearance reference in instrument procedure design.
CRT: Cathode ray tube. A display technology historically used in aircraft cockpit instruments, ATC radar scopes, and navigation displays; largely superseded by modern LCD and solid-state displays.
CS: Call sign. A unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to an aircraft, ground station, or ATC facility for radiotelephony communications; used to ensure positive identification during voice or data link exchanges.
